description: OVD-844 detector config: the SQL content rules (rls, definer) and the AGENTS.md 'Approval timing and low-risk auto-merge' safe categories. Sensitive path classes are not here: they come only from docs/sensitive-paths.json through scripts/lib/sensitive-paths.mjs (OVD-873), and this file never copies those globs. A path with any sensitive class is never in a safe category. Read by scripts/sensitive-class-detect.mjs; the auto-merge eligibility check (OVD-845) reads the detector's JSON result, not this file.

syntax.paths: Globs over the repo-relative path, compiled by the shared matcher (scripts/lib/sensitive-paths.mjs compileGlob): picomatch semantics with dot and nocase, supported syntax *, **, ? and {a,b}.
syntax.path_keywords: Path words, case-insensitive. A path splits into words on non-alphanumerics and camelCase boundaries; a keyword matches a word it prefixes ('auth' matches 'authProvider', 'auth-callback'). A hyphenated keyword matches consecutive words ('provider-admission' matches 'providerAdmission').
syntax.exclude: Globs; a path matching one is not in this entry.
syntax.exclude_keywords: Path keywords; a path matching one is not in this entry. Exclusions fail closed, so here a keyword also matches inside a word ('auth' matches 'Unauthorized', 'Reauthenticate').
syntax.sql_content: Token sequences matched in SQL after comments are removed (a -- comment ends at LF or CR, as in Postgres). As in the Postgres scanner, every code point at or above U+0080 is an identifier and dollar-tag character, so a non-ASCII character never splits an identifier ($—$...$—$ is one dollar-quoted string). A double-quoted identifier is one lower-cased word, so SET "row_security" matches. A quoted name that is not identifier-shaped keeps its quotes as part of the word, so ";", "(" or ")" never acts as a statement end or a parenthesis. E-string backslash escapes are decoded, and adjacent single-quoted strings separated by whitespace containing a newline (including -- comments) are concatenated while preserving the initial escape mode and source lines. U& token sequences conservatively add auth, including Unicode strings or identifiers with a custom UESCAPE. Every string literal and dollar-quoted body is also tokenized as SQL (DO blocks, function bodies, EXECUTE strings), so a literal that mentions a token sequence matches too (set_config('row_security', ...)); false positives are accepted to fail closed. A token is a whole lower-cased word or one punctuation character, so 'row_security' does not match 'row_security_note'. Each rule has a unique id and a reason; both appear in the result's reasons. Every changed file except a removal is read at the head. The SQL is read as data and never executed. A rule with 'within' matches only when one of those token sequences occurs earlier in the same statement (back to the previous ';', so a DO body's statements count on their own); a rule with 'after' also needs one of its token sequences earlier in the same statement; a rule with 'inside' matches only within the argument of one of its token sequences in the same top-level statement: for a sequence ending in '(' (format() up to its matching ')'), otherwise everything after it up to the end of its own statement (EXECUTE ...), counting '(' ')' and ';' only at that sequence's string nesting level and ending with the string that holds it; a rule with 'until' matches only when that token follows later in the same statement. An 'informational' rule reports its hits but never adds its class. Every hit reports its rule id, path and line.
syntax.sql_exemptions: An exemption clears a hit of one of its rules (only auth_set_role, auth_set_local_role and auth_reset_role may be listed) in a file matching its paths only when the hit's whole top-level statement, with comments removed, is exactly SET [LOCAL] ROLE followed by one of its targets unquoted and an optional ';' (auth_set_role, auth_set_local_role; targets required), or exactly RESET ROLE and an optional ';' (auth_reset_role; no targets), case-insensitive, words separated by SQL whitespace. Statements split at a ';' outside strings, quoted identifiers, dollar-quoted bodies and comments. Nothing else is exempt: a hit inside a string or dollar-quoted body (DO blocks, EXECUTE, format()), a quoted role name, trailing tokens (anon, x or anon || '_x'), set_config and any other role stay sensitive. A file holding any character the SQL tokenizer does not classify (an ASCII control character other than SQL whitespace) gets no exemption at all and fails closed: the rules also run with comments and quotes read as code, every hit is reported, the reason sql:tokenizer_unknown_char is added and the file gets every class a SQL rule can add (rls, definer, auth). Exemption paths match case-sensitively. Each exemption must set gate_loosening: true; every hit it clears is reported in the result's top-level sql_exemptions list (marked gate_loosening: true) and the job summary, and a cleared hit adds no class. Any other hit of the same rule in the same file still does.

rules.reason: CREATE POLICY defines a row level security policy
ALTER POLICY changes a row level security policy
DROP POLICY removes a row level security policy
ENABLE, DISABLE, FORCE or NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY changes whether policies apply
BYPASSRLS on CREATE/ALTER ROLE or USER (or CREATE GROUP) lets a role skip every policy
NOBYPASSRLS on CREATE/ALTER ROLE or USER changes whether a role skips policies
rolbypassrls is the catalog column behind BYPASSRLS
SET row_security (also ALTER ROLE/DATABASE/SYSTEM ... SET) changes whether policies apply
SET LOCAL row_security changes whether policies apply
SET SESSION row_security changes whether policies apply
RESET row_security changes whether policies apply
set_config('row_security', ...) changes whether policies apply
Any mention of the row_security setting fails closed, since set_config and SET can name it in many forms
SECURITY DEFINER runs a function with its owner's privileges
SET ROLE switches the current role
SET LOCAL ROLE switches the current role
SET SESSION ROLE switches the current role
SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION switches the session user
SET LOCAL SESSION AUTHORIZATION switches the session user
set_config('role', ...) switches the current role
set_config('session_authorization', ...) switches the session user
set_config(('role'), ...) switches the current role
set_config(setting_name => 'role', ...) switches the current role
set_config(setting_name := 'role', ...) switches the current role
Any mention of the session_authorization setting fails closed, since set_config can name it in many forms
RESET ROLE switches the current role back to the session user
RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION switches the session user
RESET ALL resets role, session authorization and row_security
EXECUTE or format() with the word role in its argument can build a role switch or grant at run time (execute format('set %s anon', 'role'))
EXECUTE or format() with the word roles in its argument can build a role switch or grant at run time
SUPERUSER on CREATE/ALTER ROLE or USER (or CREATE GROUP) grants every privilege
CREATEROLE on CREATE/ALTER ROLE or USER (or CREATE GROUP) lets a role create, alter and grant roles
REPLICATION on CREATE/ALTER ROLE or USER (or CREATE GROUP) lets a role stream every row, bypassing policies
NOSUPERUSER only removes a privilege; reported, not sensitive
NOCREATEROLE only removes a privilege; reported, not sensitive
NOREPLICATION only removes a privilege; reported, not sensitive
GRANT postgres TO makes a role a member of the superuser role
GRANT supabase_admin TO makes a role a member of the platform admin role
GRANT service_role TO lets a role act as service_role, which bypasses row level security
GRANT authenticator TO lets a role switch to any role authenticator can
CREATE ROLE/USER/GROUP ... IN ROLE (or IN GROUP) postgres makes the new role a member of the superuser role
CREATE ROLE/USER/GROUP ... IN ROLE (or IN GROUP) supabase_admin makes the new role a member of the platform admin role
CREATE ROLE/USER/GROUP ... IN ROLE (or IN GROUP) service_role makes the new role a member of service_role, which bypasses row level security

exemptions.reason: pgTAP tests switch to the anon or authenticated API roles with a plain top-level SET [LOCAL] ROLE statement to prove policies hold for clients; that drops privileges and changes no shipped database state. A switch to service_role, postgres, supabase_admin, authenticator or any other role in a test stays sensitive, as does any switch built in a string or DO block, and every switch outside supabase/tests/**.

pgTAP tests end a role switch with a plain top-level RESET ROLE statement. RESET ROLE only returns to the session role the test connected as, so it cannot escalate past it. RESET ROLE built in a string or DO block, and every RESET ROLE outside supabase/tests/**, stays sensitive.

rules.reason: SQL anywhere, including comments; new RPC names (unresolved names fail closed)
Migration directory on either rename side or a migration timestamp header
Changed secret or environment names, including fixtures
Send/submit indicators; GET and navigation to a new host are notes only; ambiguous network calls fail closed
Install scripts, non-npm resolved hosts, git or tarball dependencies (npm registry tarballs allowed)
Any .github path, governance/ruleset/CODEOWNERS, gate loosening, or removed job, section, test or required check
Deletion or rename of a sensitive base path

docs.description: Markdown at the repo root and docs/**. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md carry governance sections a path cannot separate, so they stay out.

frontend_ui.description: Frontend UI outside auth, session, permission, sign-in, password, billing, pricing, checkout, stripe and dispatch paths.

repo_scripts.description: Repo scripts, excluding deploy, release and secret, credential or token paths.
